summary: Active 1923 4A-style lookout on a granite dome in Sequoia National Forest, still staffed in fire season and open to climbing visitors.

facts.design: 4A style, 14 by 14 ft cab (1917-1923 design), replaced on-site by the 4AR model elsewhere; reached via a suspended flight of stairs

access.note: Staffed full-time in fire season and open to visitors who climb the stairs; one of the most-visited lookout sites in the Giant Sequoia National Monument.

visit.trail_note: Reached by trail/road to the base and then a suspended staircase up the granite dome; south of Hume Lake in the Hume Lake Ranger District.

events.note: Buck Rock established as a key fire-detection location circa 1912.
4A-style 14x14 ft lookout design in use from 1917.
Current cab built in 1923, when the 4A design was being replaced generally by the newer 4AR model; this is one of only three surviving 4A cabs.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register August 20, 1998.

evidence.supports: Established circa 1912, oldest standing cab in the forest, staffed and open to public
evidence.quote: Buck Rock was established as a key fire detection location circa 1912... It is also the oldest standing lookout in the forest, the current cab built in 1923... The lookout is staffed full-time during fire season and is generally open to the public.

evidence.supports: Location and views near Hume Lake, Kings Canyon, Sequoia parks
evidence.quote: Buck Rock is strategically perched on top of a granite dome overlooking most of the Hume Lake District, Kings Canyon National Park and Sequoia National Park.

evidence.supports: 4A design built 1917-1923, replaced by 4AR, one of three surviving, suspended stairs
evidence.quote: The 4A style 14'x 14' lookout was built from 1917 to 1923 when it was replaced by the 4AR model. Buck Rock Lookout, constructed on the Sequoia National Forest in 1923, is one of only three 4As remaining. It is reached via a suspended flight of stairs.

evidence.supports: Buck Rock Foundation preserves and runs public education, webcam
evidence.quote: Our volunteers restore and maintain historic lookout facilities so that they remain in service for fire detection and open to the public for visitation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: fire-lookouts.org gives 8,502 ft while the brief/NHLR give 8,408 ft (2,562.8 m); kept the brief's NHLR-sourced figure and did not state an elevation figure in the story to avoid asserting the disputed number.

notes_for_editor: Elevation figures disagree slightly between sources (8,408 ft brief/NHLR vs 8,502 ft fire-lookouts.org); story avoids stating a number. Did not verify current 2026 staffing status beyond fire-lookouts.org's general description of the season-staffed, public-access model, which is longstanding but not dated to this year specifically.
